problem: Loopbreaker starts at the issue, so there is nowhere to group issues into a deliverable or to hold a strategic bet above them. A multi-issue portfolio UI has no hierarchy to render. Critically, an epic also has no home for its executable scenario - the end-to-end path that says what the grouped work must actually demonstrate - so an epic can be declared complete purely because its children individually shipped, with nothing proving the whole ever ran.
appetite: One hierarchy slice with concrete typed tables, an epic executable scenario that is stored and attestable, and a portfolio read model - not Rordi's unified data-driven entity table.
smallest_slice: Add initiatives and epics tables with defined-cardinality parent edges to issues; store an executable scenario on the epic and require an attestation that it ran; make the epic completion gate require both every child issue shipping-ready and that scenario attestation; and expose a portfolio read model of initiative to epic to issue with per-tier disposition covering orphans and empty parents.
non_goals: Rordi's unified entities table and data-driven schemas
Building the portfolio UI itself (this only unblocks it)
Nesting beyond initiative to epic to issue
Automatic execution of the scenario - this slice stores it and records an attestation that it ran
success_signal: Issues imported under an epic report as its children through the named construction surface; an epic with unshipped children or without a recorded scenario attestation reads blocked with the exact blocking ids, an epic with no children reads empty and never complete, and only an epic whose children are all shipping-ready AND whose executable scenario is attested reads complete; the portfolio read model returns the full hierarchy including orphaned issues.
reversibility: The tiers are additive and issues remain valid standalone with no epic parent, so dropping the tables and the portfolio read model returns issue behavior exactly to its current state with no data loss.

risks.risk: Hierarchy complicates the clean single-issue substrate.
risks.mitigation: Leave the issue substrate untouched and add a separate portfolio read model.

risks.risk: Requiring a scenario attestation could block epics whose children have all shipped.
risks.mitigation: That is the intended semantics - an unattested scenario is precisely the gap this slice exists to close - and the blocked disposition names the missing attestation explicitly.
